questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code validates incoming telemetry batches? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A batch contains 501 well-formed readings for a valid deviceId. What is the outcome?
choices: The first 500 are stored and the last is dropped
The request reaches the loop in ingest() and is rejected with 422
All 501 are stored because @Size only applies to strings
The request is rejected with 400 and a fields map before the controller method body runs

questions.prompt: Why is the "recordedAt must not be in the future" rule implemented in the controller rather than as an annotation on ReadingDto?
choices: The limit depends on the current time from an injected Clock, which a static annotation cannot express, and the controller returns 422 rather than the 400 used for shape errors
Annotations cannot be applied to Instant fields
Bean Validation runs after the controller method, so time checks must come first
Because @Valid skips fields of type Instant

questions.prompt: A request whose deviceId is "sensor 01" (containing a space) and whose readings list is empty is submitted. What does the client receive?
choices: A 202 because the service only uses deviceId as a string prefix
A 400 whose fields map contains entries for both deviceId and readings
A 400 whose fields map contains only deviceId, because validation stops at the first violation
